title: Feature Extraction vs Fine‑Tuning 🔧
description: Understand the two main transfer learning strategies and how to implement them.

slides.title: Two Paths to Adapt a Pre‑trained Model 🛤️
slides.content:
# 1. Feature Extraction
Freeze the convolutional base, use its output as features for a new classifier. Only the new classifier is trained.

# 2. Fine‑Tuning
Unfreeze some top layers of the base model and train them together with the new classifier. This adapts the pre‑trained features to the new task.

> Analogy: Feature extraction = using a pre‑built camera to take pictures and only changing how you interpret them. Fine‑tuning = also adjusting the camera's lens slightly for your specific scene.

slides.title: Feature Extraction in Code
slides.content: Set `layer.trainable = False` for all layers in the base model.
slides.codeSnippet:
base_model = VGG16(weights='imagenet', include_top=False)
for layer in base_model.layers:
    layer.trainable = False

# Now add new classifier head
global_avg = GlobalAveragePooling2D()(base_model.output)
predictions = Dense(5, activation='softmax')(global_avg)
model = Model(inputs=base_model.input, outputs=predictions)

quizData.question: In feature extraction, which layers are updated during training?

options.text: All layers of the base model
Only the newly added classifier layers

quizData.explanation: The base model is frozen; gradients only flow through the new head, updating its weights.

slides.title: Fine‑Tuning: Unfreeze and Retrain Selectively 🔓
slides.content:
# Steps for Fine‑Tuning
1. First, train the new classifier head with the base frozen (feature extraction).
2. Then, unfreeze some top layers of the base model.
3. Recompile with a very low learning rate (to avoid wrecking pre‑trained weights).
4. Train end‑to‑end.

This allows the pre‑trained features to shift slightly to your domain.

slides.title: Fine‑Tuning Example
slides.content: Unfreeze the last few layers of the base model.
slides.codeSnippet:
# After initial training with head only
base_model.trainable = True

# Freeze all layers except the last 5
for layer in base_model.layers[:-5]:
    layer.trainable = False

model.compile(optimizer=Adam(learning_rate=1e-5), loss='categorical_crossentropy', metrics=['accuracy'])
model.fit(train_data, epochs=5)

slides.title: Don't Fine‑Tune Too Aggressively ⚠️
slides.content: If you unfreeze too many layers with a high learning rate, you may destroy the valuable pre‑trained features. Always use a learning rate 10‑100× smaller than the initial head training.
